traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and explicit requirements for story 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are fully implemented and verified.
Summary by acceptance criteria: - **Rule Naming (REQ-RULE-NAME)**: Implemented via `src/index.ts`, which exposes `traceability/prefer-supports-annotation` as the primary rule and `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` as a deprecated alias with `meta.deprecated = true` and `meta.replacedBy = ["prefer-supports-annotation"]`. Tests exercise both rule names and they behave identically. - **Optional Warning (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING)**: `processComment` reports `preferImplements` only when both `@story` and `@req` are present; presets leave the rule disabled by default. Tests validate this behavior. - **Auto-fix Support (REQ-AUTO-FIX)**: `buildImplementsAutoFix` + `applyImplementsReplacement` implement a conservative auto-fix converting `@story`+`@req` into a single `@supports` line when safe. Multiple tests verify the concrete output. - **Single Story Conversion (REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX)**: Auto-fix requires exactly one distinct story path and one @story line; it aggregates all simple @req IDs onto the @supports line. Tests confirm multi-req behavior. - **Multi-story Detection (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT)**: Multi-story and mixed `@supports` cases are detected and reported with `multiStoryDetected` or `cannotAutoFix` and never auto-fixed, as required and covered by tests. - **Preserve Order / Format (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT)**: The replacement preserves indentation and `*` markers and only substitutes/removes the specific `@story`/@req lines, so the relative positioning of other tags (e.g., `@param`) is maintained. This matches the examples in the story and the intended semantics. - **Configurable Enforcement (REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY)**: Rule is absent from both `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` (default off) and can be configured with standard ESLint severities for both primary and alias keys; tests explicitly validate this. - **Both Formats Valid (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION)**: Legacy `@story`/`@req` usage remains valid when the rule is disabled; even when enabled, patterns like only-@story, only-@req, or only-@supports are ignored by this rule. Combined with the existing core rules, this ensures continued validation of both formats. - **Quality Standards / Valid Output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT)**: Auto-fix only runs on simple, unambiguous patterns and emits `@supports` lines conforming to the formats validated by `valid-annotation-format` and `valid-req-reference`; complex cases emit warnings without fixes. Related rule tests and full test suite passing confirm this. - **Documentation**: README and `user-docs/migration-guide.md` provide a clear migration guide, examples of before/after transformations, opt‑in configuration, and rule/alias naming, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
All targeted and full test runs pass, and the implementation matches both the story’s functional requirements and its design/behavioral narrative. Therefore, this story is fully implemented: **PASSED**.
